items.prompt:
A fact, example, or statistic that backs a point is called:
A) evidence
B) a title
C) a guess

steps: Supports the point. Key is A.

items.prompt:
Read.

Kids should sleep more. Studies show rested kids score higher.

The author's main point is:
A) Kids should sleep more
B) Tests are hard
C) Sleep is nice

A statement that tells WHY is a:
A) reason
B) picture
C) heading

Read.

Our city should build bike lanes. One city that did reduced car trips by 20%.

Which EVIDENCE supports that bikes cut traffic?
A) Our city should build bike lanes
B) One city reduced car trips by 20%
C) Bikes are fun
items.answer: B) One city reduced car trips by 20%

solution.answer: B) One city reduced car trips by 20%

items.prompt:
Read.

We need recycling bins. Last month our school threw away 200 pounds of paper.

The '200 pounds' fact is:
A) evidence for needing bins
B) a reason not to recycle
C) unrelated

steps: Data supports the point. Key is A.

items.prompt:
Which gives the STRONGEST support for a point?
A) a statistic from a study
B) 'because I think so'
C) a joke
items.answer: A) a statistic from a study

steps: Data is strong evidence. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) a statistic from a study

items.prompt:
Read.

Our school should start later. First, teens need more sleep; sleep experts recommend 9 hours. Second, later starts improve grades; one district saw test scores rise.

Which evidence supports the GRADES point?
A) sleep experts recommend 9 hours
B) one district saw test scores rise
C) teens need more sleep
items.answer: B) one district saw test scores rise

steps: Matches the grades point. Key is B.
solution.answer: B) one district saw test scores rise

items.prompt:
Why do authors connect each piece of evidence to a specific point?
A) so readers can see exactly how each point is supported
B) to make the text longer
C) to confuse readers
items.answer: A) so readers can see exactly how each point is supported

steps: Evidence should back specific points. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) so readers can see exactly how each point is supported
